validity.researcher_notes:
Checked all four units hanging off this ref (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Location), all cited to https://liting.uz/page/4. That page's title is "AO 'O'ZLITINEFTGAZ'" (a design-institute 'История института'/history page), and it is a bare client-rendered React SPA: our fetch and a WebFetch pass both confirm the served HTML has no text content beyond the company name (JS never executes for a scraper), so it cannot actually be read to confirm it names Mubarek-Kagan. This matches the worklist's own existing_ref_checks, which already flagged the Status value 'operating' as not found on the page; Fuel/PipelineType/Location were marked ok only because the URL is reachable (200), with value_checked=false — i.e. never actually content-verified either. Also checked gem.wiki's other three cited sources for this page (UNDP gas-transport-system-diagram PDF, cyberleninka gas-geopolitics PDF, utg.uz shareholder-structure page) with url_verifier: none of the four sources gem.wiki cites for this row contain the strings 'Мубарек' or 'Каган' when checked, so none independently supports this specific segment as cited.

EXISTENCE, however, is independently confirmed: Мубарекнефтегазмонтаж (Mubarekneftegazmontazh), a major Uzbek gas-construction contractor unrelated to GEM, lists 'газопровод «Мубарек - Каган»' by name among the main production facilities ('основные производственные объекты') it has built/serviced, in the same sentence as other verifiably real Uzbek gas trunks (Sazakino-Nukus, the Mubarek gas-processing plant, the Khodjaabad UGS) — http://www.mngmaj.uz/about/index.htm. Separately, Uztransgaz's own site (utg.uz) confirms both named endpoints are live operational hubs in its network: the 'Kagan Department of Main Gas Pipelines' (Каганское УМГ) is an active field unit (2022 seasonal-preparation press item), and the 'Muborak Main Gas Pipeline Plant' compressor shop is under Uztransgaz jurisdiction — consistent with, though not an explicit naming of, a Mubarek-Kagan trunk between them. Only ONE source (mngmaj.uz) explicitly names this exact pipeline, so this is medium tier, not high — extensive further Russian-language searching (Uzbekneftegaz/Uztransgaz pages, Soviet gas-industry terms, ru.wikipedia for Uztransgaz and for the Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty pipeline, oilcapital.ru, cyberleninka) did not surface a second source naming it directly.

CLASSIFICATION: transmission trunk between two Uztransgaz hub cities is consistent with the recorded PipelineType=transmission — no concern.

DUPLICATE check against the roster: P6965 (segment I, 'Газопровод "Мубарек-Каган", 1-ая нитка' = '1st string') and its sibling P6966 (segment II, '2-ая нитка' = '2nd string') are a normal twin-parallel-line pattern, same shape as Gazli-Kagan I-IV — not a duplicate. SPEC: Diameter and Capacity are blank with no ref, and I could not find either specifically for Mubarek-Kagan despite searching. One Kagan-UMG press item describes a 720mm-to-1020mm pipe replacement, but that almost certainly refers to Gazli-Kagan (whose roster diameters are 720/1020mm), not Mubarek-Kagan — deliberately NOT attributed here to avoid a false fill. LengthKnown is correctly blank; LengthEstimateKm=99.93 is a schematic straight-line route estimate (RouteAccuracy 'very low'), not a researched length, so nothing to verify there. Owner/Parent are blank ('unknown') on the sheet — no independent source found naming an operator/owner distinct from Uztransgaz generally, so left as-is rather than guessed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is a Soviet-era operational trunk (twin lines feeding the Kagan gas hub from the Mubarek gas complex), not a stalled proposed/under-construction project, so the dormancy-inference rules (2y/4y) do not apply here — 'stale' would misclassify a long-running in-service asset as it would a shelved proposal. Uztransgaz's own site (utg.uz) confirms the 'Kagan Department of Main Gas Pipelines' is an active field unit still doing seasonal operational prep (dated press item, Sept 2022) and that the 'Muborak Main Gas Pipeline Plant' remains under Uztransgaz jurisdiction (undated but current corporate page, fetched 2026-08-26) — i.e. both endpoints are live, staffed, operating parts of the network today, not decommissioned. mngmaj.uz's project-history listing corroborates the pipeline as a real built facility. No independent evidence of a status change, closure, or replacement was found in Russian- or English-language searching. Recorded Status='operating' stands; LastUpdated (2024-09-13) is not stale enough to warrant a change verdict, and no newer dated evidence of a status change exists to act on.
